By: Diana Lucas | Production

Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
George Bizos Obit
George Bizoz passed away on 9th September this week
President Cyril Ramaphosa announced the death in a televised news briefing. No cause was given, but he said Mr. Bizos’s health had recently begun to fail.
Over a long and combative career, Mr. Bizos was one of only a handful of lawyers who sought redress for victims of racial separation through the very legal system that sanctioned it. While deeply flawed by the pervasive prejudice of the times, South Africa’s legal establishment did offer some slim protection to the accused under a white minority regime that liked to boast of a commitment to Western values.
While many of his trials were fought in the glare of publicity, which he often sought to exploit, Mr. Bizos claimed a particular contribution to the destiny of his adoptive land by urging Mr. Mandela to insert three words — “if needs be” — into his oft-cited address from the dock at the so-called Rivonia trial of leaders of the African National Congress in the early 1960s.
In his first draft, Mr. Bizos said, Mr. Mandela had written that he was prepared to die for “the ideal of a democratic and free society in which all persons live together in harmony and with equal opportunities.”
Indeed, from 2012 to 2015 he was among the lawyers who represented the familie of Marikana — bloodletting that he likened to atrocities of the apartheid era.
who died in police custody in 1977.


Further information:
In hearings called by South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission in the 1990s, Mr. Bizos represented the families of leading foes of apartheid, including Matthew Goniwe, an educator who was one of three activists murdered by the police in 1985. They were known as the Cradock Four, named for the small, segregated township in the Eastern Cape region where they had built a challenge to white rule.
In the early 1990s, Mr. Bizos joined other lawyers in court proceedings to formally approve South Africa’s post-apartheid constitution, regarded as one of the most liberal in the world.
He acted as an independent barrister for many years, but from 1991 onward he was associated with the Legal Resources Center, a prominent firm of human rights lawyers in Johannesburg of which he became senior counsel. Mr. Bizos also worked in Botswana and Zimbabwe, where he defended Morgan Tsvangirai the opposition leader, against treason charges in 2003.

An obit to honour the late George Bizos, with past footage and interviews with Terror Lekota, Judge Moseneke and others

Script:



Mandela interviewed 2001
Mandela: “On my last day I want those who honour me to be able to say ‘Here lies a man who has done his duty to his country and his people. George Bizos will get that type of response.’”

V/O
Bizo’s defining moment, a moment imprinted into South Africa’s destiny, was his defence of his client and friend, Nelson Mandela, in the 1964 Rivonia trial.

Mandela: And People like George Bizos were there defending us. We really turned the court against our prosecutors.

V/O
Historians of the trial maintain that Bizos’ insertion of the three words, ‘If needs be’, into Mandela’s final address, led to Mandela and his fellow trialists escaping the death penalty.
Mandela, Speech UP SOUND But if needs be, it is an ideal for which I am prepared to die.”
V/O
At 13 years old George, with his father fled the Nazi occupation of Greece.

George: We arrived in Durban, I saw black man torn vests barefooted pulling heavy rickshaws, I said to myself as poor as some of us may have been in Greece at least we had animals to do that sort of work.

V/O
Friend and relation Aki Anastasio

Aki Anastasiou: He was a real story teller, he would remember things from the day he arrived in SA and he would recall stuff from his village in Greece … He was the most incredibly principled man he always had time for people he always gave of himself no matter who you were he would dedicate the conversation to speaking to you.

V/O
After scraping together the tuition money George Bizos managed to get into the law faculty at the University of Witwatersrand,

Bizos I became politicised at University

V/O
In the 1950’s and 60’s Bizos became a tireless champion of those that suffered under the security forces, victims of apartheid, political activists

V/O
Colleague, Judge Dikgang Moseneke

Moseneke He was near fearless Being a struggle lawyer you could be killed so it was dangerous.

V/O
In 1985, he was the advocate in the Delmas trial, the longest trial in the history of South Africa … Mosiuoa Lekota was one of the 22 indited for treason.

Mosiuoa ‘Terror’ Lekota
Terror: You’ve never seen anyone like him we soon realised he was one of our comrades his main expertise was cross examination He just destroyed them witness after witness.

Dikgang Moseneke: Just think about it Steve Biko is murdered in a cell George Bizos is there to do the inquest Neil Agett is killed again by the police in a cell Bizos is there Marikana happens and George Bizos is there You can go On and on and he retires from formal practice and goes to the legal Resources Centre and goes to work for those who need most attention and our deprived in our society so he had a rudder of right and wrong.

V/O
Bizos’s passion was education and in 1974 he took the lead in establishing a Hellenic School, SAHETI that in the dark days of apartheid was open to all.
Aki: I spent my whole life there and he would be at every single event he was the father of the school.
Warwick Taylor
Executive Head SAHETI
He was kind and warm it didn’t matter who you were he took time to engage and to hear your story and there is an aspect of who he was will always be embedded here even trees on property he planted he would sit down on a bench and the children would come and sit around him and he would engage with them and try and make the links within the community.
V/O
Bizos spent 30 years at the Legal Resources Centre, fighting for the rights of the underdog and mentoring young lawyers coming through the system

Claire: What were his interactions like?
Nersan Govender
National Director: Legal Resources Centre

Nersan: George was a giant among giants, he was a man with a lot of humility…time to talk to everyone//// he meeting a long lost friend.//

V/O
On the day of Mandela’s inauguration in 1994 Bizos was a special guest

Bizos: Down below were thousands of thousands watching the special ceremony….. and snaked her way through the helicopters…salute the new president.
V/O
But in his later years after Mandela’s Death in 2013 and Ahmed Kathrada in 2017, Bizos became became disillusioned and disappointed in South Africa’s swerve to corruption
Nersan: there were many times he cried and tears about how the country has turned out this way not what was promised he felt very strongly about that He said no one to blame is no longer proper finding…Zondo line will responsible someone has to blame

V/O
A tireless defender of the defenceless, a lover of life, Bizos might have adopted South Africa as his own but his Mediterranean roots were embedded in his way of life. Much of his precious time was spent with his wife , three sons and grandchildren at home and in their garden – his sanctuary.

Aki He loved talking about his vegetable garden that was his pride and joy.

Nasan: He would go and
Moseneke: You hit is home chop fresh vegetables from his garden think about that and the …….. Think about that and the symbolism around sharing salads .. bring a salad for the accused. So he had incredible humanity.

Aki: A few years ago it was the launch of his book and I was asked to read one of his favourite poems called Ithaca…and the poem talks about this is his journey back home to Ithaca after mass wars in troy and the challenges he has going back home he eventually went home but the journey was the most important part of it and that symbolise Adv George Bizoz’s life

V/O WE NEED TO WRITE SOME OF RAMAPHOSA WORDS OVER THE VISUALS HIGHLIGHTD BELOW my suggestion below we can use less
On Friday, it was announced George Bizos would be given a Category 1 Funeral. In President Ramaphosa’s words….He was one of the architects of our constitution we dip our heads in honour of the contribution he made to our democracy…
